liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jack Straw, Brokedown Palace, and the China Cat to Rider transition are standard bearers [11]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Tennessee Jed is actually intense, unlike its usual funny nature [21]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The transition from China Cat Sunflower to I Know You Rider is a highlight [15]
- **Eyes of the World** (1 review): The first slipknot jam occurs at the end of Eyes of the World [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-10-20.170419.aud.Conner.gems.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 31 songs; 255 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd74-10-20.sbd.finney.229.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 30 songs; 237 min; rated 4.19/5 by 21 [3]. Said about its sound: Recording is very clean, though a bit of crowd noise would reveal the evening's intensity; Sound quality degrades after Eyes of the World, with an over-emphasis on the bass; Mississippi Half Step sounds too fast, tinny, and nasal, though the performance is lovely [11][12][14]
- **gd1974-10-20.176674.sony.ecm250.falanga.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 31 songs; 239 min [4]
- **gd1974-10-20.sbd.smith-lee.GEMS.97193.flac16**: soundboard; 29 songs; 234 min; rated 3.64/5 by 14 [8]

## Around the show

- Mickey Hart was brought in for the show, described as being sprung from the mental institution [15]
- The band melted the remaining ice in the old skating rink that night [17]
- The show marks the end of an era, though the patchwork quality can be jarring [19]
- The band considered retiring, thinking this might be their last concert, and wanted to go out high [21]
- Mickey Hart returns to drums and percussion for set two, Sugar Magnolia, and Johnny B. Goode [1]
- This show blows the 19th out of the water, despite occasional tinny sound [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-10-20.170419.aud.Conner.gems.flac2496**: taped by Charles Conner; transferred by Transferred and mastered by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: Sony ECM-22P mic (mono) > Sony TC-55 > Maxell UD C-90 cassettes [1]. Also: First known master audience source, from Charles Conner cassettes, aired on KXCI Tucson in 2024 [1]
- **gd74-10-20.sbd.finney.229.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Mixed sources via D. Finney, stemming from Frank's Picks tree, with some material from the show [3]
- **gd1974-10-20.176674.sony.ecm250.falanga.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Louis Falanga; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Louis Falanga's Master Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM 250 mic > Sony TC-110 (Maxell UD C120) [4]
- **gd1974-10-20.sbd.smith-lee.GEMS.97193.flac16**: transferred by Matt Smith and Jamie Waddell; source: Multitrack MR>2 track mixdown>?R>R>CD [8]. Also: Real-time multi-track mix on black Maxell UDII tape, transferred by Matt Smith from Pat Lee tapes [8]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Winterland Arena - October 20, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/october-20-1974) [23]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Winterland Arena - October 20, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/october-20-1974) [24]
